import { Aside, Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import SeqDiagram from '../../../../components/SeqDiagram.astro';

**Task:** call the methods of an app you deployed, from a web page, a script,
a service or the command line, and read its events as they happen.

Every client does the same five things, which is why you use one of the
Calimero clients rather than plain HTTP:

1. **Attest** the node: fetch its TDX quote and check it against a policy you
   give (the signed mero-tee release it names, at least a minimum version) before
   sending anything.
2. **Seal** every request end to end to the attested key (Noise,
   `calimero/sealed-http/v2`), so nothing between you and the enclave reads it.
3. **Authenticate** with a passkey session (people) or an API key (machines).
4. **Call** the app's routes: `POST /apps/{app}/intents` for a logged call,
   `POST /apps/{app}/views` for a read, `GET /apps/{app}/events` for the event stream.
5. **Retry** a call the node answered `503` with the same idempotency key, so it
   runs once even if the first attempt committed.

| Client | Where | Package |
| --- | --- | --- |
| mero-js | browser, Node 18+ | `@calimero-network/mero-js` ([docs](https://calimero-network.github.io/mero-js/)) |
| calimero-client-py | CPython 3.9+ | `calimero-client-py` ([docs](https://calimero-network.github.io/calimero-client-py/)) |
| calimero-client | Rust | `crates/client` in this repository |
| meroctl | the command line | `crates/meroctl` ([reference](/operate/meroctl/)) |

All four send the same requests over the same sealed channel. For methods and
types generated from your app's ABI on top of mero-js or the Python client,
see [Typed clients for your app](/build/guides/typed-clients/).

## Connect and sign in

<Tabs>
<TabItem label="mero-js">

```ts
import { CalimeroClient, browserPasskey } from '@calimero-network/mero-js';

// A Calimero Cloud cluster by name: its nodes come from the public directory,
// and each is attested under your policy before anything is sent.
const client = await CalimeroClient.connect({
  cluster: 'eu-shared-1',
  policy: { release: { minReleaseVersion: '2.3.109' } },
});
// Or nodes you name: new CalimeroClient({ baseUrl, nodes, policy }).
// A development cluster (merod local, merod run --dev): policy: { allowMock: true }.

await client.signIn(browserPasskey());   // a person, in a browser
client.useApiKey('cal_...');             // or a machine
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Python">

```python
from calimero_client_py import Client

client = Client.connect("eu-shared-1", tee_profiles=["<profile>"])
# Or one node: Client("https://node1.example.com", tee_profiles=[...]);
# a development cluster: Client("http://127.0.0.1:2501", allow_mock=True).
client.use_api_key("cal_...")
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Rust">

```rust
use calimero_client::{Client, Measurements, Policy};

let policy = Policy {
    measurements: Measurements::Release {
        allowed_profiles: vec!["<profile>".to_owned()],
        min_version: None, // 2.3.109 when none is given
    },
    ..Policy::default()   // allow_mock: true for a development cluster
};
let client = Client::connect("https://node1.example.com", policy)?;
client.use_api_key(&std::env::var("CALIMERO_API_KEY")?).await;
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="meroctl">

```bash
meroctl node add eu https://node1.example.com
export CALIMERO_TEE_PROFILES=<profile> CALIMERO_API_KEY=cal_...
meroctl --node eu whoami
# A development cluster: meroctl node add local http://127.0.0.1:2501 --allow-mock
#                        meroctl login --dev-passkey ./me.passkey
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

- **Passkeys** are for people, in a browser (`browserPasskey()`); a passkey
  belongs to one cluster, and one made elsewhere is
  `401 PASSKEY_UNKNOWN_HERE`. A page served from the app's own frontend gets
  a session bound to its package: see [Ship a frontend](/build/guides/frontends/).
- **API keys** are for scripts and services. An account holder creates one
  with a passkey step-up (`meroctl account api-key create [--context C]...
  [--read-only] [--ttl-secs N]`, or `client.auth.apikeyCreate` in mero-js);
  the key is shown once. `--context` limits it to some apps and `--read-only`
  to views.
- Sessions refresh themselves: a `401` on a session the client holds the
  refresh token of is refreshed once and the request sent again.
- `421 WRONG_NODE` means the node runs a release the account's owners have
  not approved. mero-js and the Python client move to the next node they were
  given; the Rust client returns `Error::WrongNode` for you to do so.

## Call and read

<Tabs>
<TabItem label="mero-js">

```ts
const { index, result, events } = await client.apps.call({
  app, method: 'set', args: { key: 'a', value: '1' }, idempotencyKey: 'set-a-1',
});
const { result: value } = await client.apps.view({ app, method: 'get', args: { key: 'a' } });
const fast = await client.apps.view({ app, method: 'get', args: { key: 'a' }, consistency: 'stale', minIndex: index });
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Python">

```python
r = client.apps.call(app=app_id, method="set", args={"key": "a", "value": "1"},
                     idempotency_key="set-a-1")
v = client.apps.view(app=app_id, method="get", args={"key": "a"}).to_dict()["result"]
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Rust">

```rust
use serde_json::json;

let set = client
    .apps()
    .call(&app, "set", Some(json!({ "key": "a", "value": "1" })), Some("set-a-1"), None)
    .await?;
let got = client
    .apps()
    .view(&app, "get", Some(json!({ "key": "a" })), None, None)
    .await?;
println!("{} at {}", got.result, got.index);
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="meroctl">

```bash
meroctl call -c my-kv set --args '{"key":"a","value":"1"}' --idempotency-key set-a-1
meroctl call -c my-kv get --args '{"key":"a"}' --view
meroctl call -c my-kv get --args '{"key":"a"}' --view --min-index 42
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

- **Names and arguments are the ABI's**: methods in camelCase, arguments a
  JSON object keyed by camelCase parameter names (`{}` for none; unknown keys
  are refused). `u64` and `i64` go as decimal strings and bytes as base64url
  without padding, in both directions ([App interface](/build/app-abi/)).
- **A call** answers `{ index, result, events, receipt }`: the log index it
  committed at, the method's result, the events of that call the caller may
  see, and the answering node's signed receipt. Arguments are at most 512 KiB
  (`413 ARGS_TOO_LARGE`).
- **A view** is linearizable by default (`consistency: "strong"`): the replica answering it first applies the index the app's leader names.
  `stale` reads the node you reached, and `minIndex` makes it wait until it
  has applied that index (`503 NOT_CAUGHT_UP` if it has not), which is how a
  client reads its own write cheaply.
- **Idempotency.** A call with a key is answered once: yours is kept 24
  hours, and mero-js and the Rust client make one when you give none (kept 10
  minutes). They resend a call with the same key while the node answers `503`
  or cannot be reached (6 retries from 200 ms doubling to 2 s; mero-js then
  moves to its next node); the Python client leaves such a node for its next one. A call
  that did commit is answered from its record, never run twice. Give your own
  key when the call must not repeat across restarts of your program.
- **Calling an action** (`#[app::action]`) only starts it: the result is
  `{ "actionId": "a.…" }` and the work happens later on the leader
  ([Timers and actions](/build/guides/timers-and-actions/)).

### Confirm methods

A method marked `#[app::confirm]` needs the caller's passkey on every call:
the node answers `412 CONFIRM_REQUIRED` with a challenge over that exact call,
and the client sends it again with the assertion, which is logged as consent.
An API key cannot answer it.

```ts
import { passkeyConfirm, browserPasskey } from '@calimero-network/mero-js';
await client.apps.call({ app, method: 'clear', args: {} }, { confirm: passkeyConfirm(browserPasskey()) });
```

```python
client.use_passkey(passkey)                                   # answers each 412
client.apps.call(app=app_id, method="clear", args={})
```

In Rust the last argument of `apps().call` is `Some(&mut passkey)`; `meroctl
call` takes `--dev-passkey FILE` on a development cluster.

## Errors

| Status, code | Meaning | mero-js |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422 APP_ERROR` | the app refused: `details.code` is the `#[app::error]` variant (or the node's ABI check: `UnknownMethod`, `WrongKind`, `NotAView`, `Forbidden`, `ConfirmRequired`), `details.fields` its fields | `AppError` (`appCode`, `fields`) |
| `422 TRAP` | the run trapped (`details.kind`: out of fuel, host denied, ...); nothing was written | `TrapError` |
| `401 UNAUTHENTICATED` | no or expired credential, or an anonymous call of a method that is not `public` | `LoginRequired` |
| `404 NOT_FOUND` | no such app, or one you may not reach (the same answer) | `NotFound` |
| `412 CONFIRM_REQUIRED` | a confirm method, sent without a passkey assertion | `ConfirmRequired` |
| `413 ARGS_TOO_LARGE` | arguments over 512 KiB | `ArgsTooLarge` |
| `403 FORBIDDEN` | a read-only team member's call that would write, or a credential that may not do this | `CalimeroError` |
| `429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | the app's developer is over its fuel for the day | `QuotaExceeded` |
| `503` | the node could not serve it now (`NOT_CAUGHT_UP`, no leader, a timeout); the clients retry | `UnavailableError` (`committed`: `false` or `'unknown'`) |
| `400 RESERVED_METHOD` | a method name starting `__` | `CalimeroError` |

Python raises `CloudError(message, status, code, details)` and Rust returns
`Error::Api { status, code, .. }`; `meroctl` prints the code and message.
The app's own error codes and fields are in its ABI (`meroctl context abi`).

## Follow events

`GET /apps/{app}/events?from=N` is a server-sent event stream: the committed
events from log index `N`, then live ones, each sent only to the accounts its
audience names. Read the state with a view, then follow from the view's
`index + 1`, so you miss nothing and see nothing twice.

<Tabs>
<TabItem label="mero-js">

```ts
const stop = new AbortController();
for await (const { id, kind, data } of client.events(app, index + 1, stop.signal)) {
  console.log(id, kind, data);
}
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Python">

```python
for e in client.events(app_id, start=index + 1, limit=100, timeout=5):
    print(e["id"], e["kind"], e["data"])
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Rust">

```rust
use futures_util::StreamExt;

let mut events = Box::pin(client.events(&app, set.index + 1).await?);
while let Some((id, kind, data)) = events.next().await {
    println!("{id} {kind} {data}");
}
```

</TabItem>
<TabItem label="meroctl">

```bash
meroctl context watch my-kv --from 0 --limit 10
```

</TabItem>
</Tabs>

A node serves at most 4,096 event and presence streams together
(`429 RATE_LIMITED` past that). What the app emits and who receives it:
[Emit events](/build/guides/events/). Live state that is not an event, such as
cursors: [Show who is here](/build/guides/presence/).

## Check a receipt

Every call and view answer carries `receipt { app, index, resultHash, node,
key, signature }`: the answering node's Ed25519 signature over the app, the
index and the SHA-256 of the result's canonical JSON. A receipt proves the
result to someone else, later, offline, but only under a key the app's
replicas attest: `verify_app_cluster` attests every replica over a fresh nonce
and answers their receipt keys and the cluster's governance.

```rust
let cluster = client.verify_app_cluster(&app).await?;
let key = cluster.keys.get(&set.receipt.node).expect("an attested replica");
assert!(set.receipt.verify(key, &set.result));
```

Python has `client.verify_app_cluster(app)`, and `meroctl attest -c CONTEXT`
prints the same.

<Aside type="note">
  The Rust snippets on this page compile against `crates/client`; the mero-js
  and Python ones use the methods those clients generate from the node's API
  document, named in their READMEs.
</Aside>
